now.detail: Guests run the original guest AI. Next: thoughts and inventory in the guest panel, eating and drinking, seating, restrooms, trash, donation boxes.

milestones.title: Phase 0: Foundations
milestones.detail: Game archives, 3D models (.nif and .bfb, 5,374 files), textures, skeletal animations (10,626 files), all 107 animal species animating, object catalog with real names, icons and prices, asset viewer, sandbox, progress page.

milestones.title: Phase 1: Terrain and world
milestones.detail: Original maps with real heights, ground painted the original way, cliffs, water; tools: raise, lower, smooth, flatten, biome paint, add/remove water; all edits saved per map. Still to compare with the original: cliff rock rule, camera controls.

milestones.title: Phase 2: Building the zoo
milestones.detail: Placement rules (grid, footprints, slopes, rotation, overlap); fences of every type and height, the fence drawing tool, gates; paths of every type, path drawing; buildings (food stands, drinks, restrooms, gift shops, shelters); scenery, benches, trash cans, lamps; plants and rocks; selling and demolishing; undo/redo. Left for later after your check: rounded path corners, curved fences, elevated paths.

milestones.title: Phase 3: Running the zoo
milestones.detail: Zoo entrance and parking; opening and closing the zoo; game clock and speeds; admission price; money, finances and the finance panel; fame/zoo rating stars; research and unlocking (Endangered Species); donation boxes; awards. Parts that need guests (admission income, fame changes, front gate upgrades) switch on in Phase 5.

milestones.title: Phase 4: Animals
milestones.detail: Adopting animals; exhibit detection (enclosed by fences); exhibit status (biome match, foliage, rocks, elevation, space, crowding, water); animal needs (hunger, thirst, rest, hygiene, privacy, exercise, social, stimulation); the original behaviors from the .tsk/.beh files (eating, drinking, sleeping, playing, grooming, fighting, hunting, swimming); shelters, food and water containers, enrichment toys; babies and breeding; sickness and recovery; escapes through broken fences; releasing to the wild.

milestones.title: Phase 5: Guests
milestones.detail: Guests arriving from the entrance; adults, children, teens, elderly; walking the paths; watching animals and viewing areas; children running to playgrounds, toys and animals; needs (hunger, thirst, restroom, energy, fun); buying food and souvenirs; litter; thoughts and complaints; donations; leaving the zoo; guest info panel.

milestones.title: Phase 6: Staff
milestones.detail: Hiring and firing; zookeepers (feeding, cleaning exhibits, healing); maintenance workers (cleaning litter, fixing fences); educators; tour guides; scientists (Endangered Species); trainers (Marine Mania); work zones; salaries.

milestones.title: Phase 7: Transport, tours and shows
milestones.detail: Skyfari, elevated tram, jeep tours (African Adventure), boat tours, marine animal shows (Marine Mania), ticket prices.

milestones.title: Phase 8: Walk-around modes
milestones.detail: Zoo Walk (first person as a guest); ZooKeeper mode (do the keeper jobs yourself); photo mode and camera.

milestones.title: Phase 9: Menus and interface
milestones.detail: Main menu, map selection, in-game toolbars and build menus, info panels, notifications, options, Zoopedia, saving and loading, all rebuilt from the original UI files.

milestones.title: Phase 10: Game modes
milestones.detail: Original maps with real heights, ground painted the original way, cliffs, water; tools: raise, lower, smooth, flatten, biome paint, add/remove water; all edits saved per map. Still to compare with the original: cliff rock rule, camera controls.

milestones.title: Phase 11: Expansion features
milestones.detail: Original maps with real heights, ground painted the original way, cliffs, water; tools: raise, lower, smooth, flatten, biome paint, add/remove water; all edits saved per map. Still to compare with the original: cliff rock rule, camera controls.

needs.title: Rounded path corners
needs.detail: In the original game, do path corners become rounded on their own when you build an L turn, or only after clicking a corner with the path tool? The game has rounded corner masks (pathcurves.xml) and I want to trigger them the same way.

needs.title: Length of a day
needs.detail: In the original game, about how many real minutes does one full day and night take? From the game data I believe one day/night cycle is one in-game month and lasts about 12 minutes. If you remember it differently, tell me.

needs.title: How animals behave
needs.detail: When you have time: watch an exhibit in our game and tell me what looks different from the original (how often animals move, eat, sleep, how fast they get hungry).

log.text: Guests use the zoo: hungry and thirsty guests buy burgers and sodas at the stands (paying the stand price), then eat and drink standing or sitting on benches; tired guests rest on benches, guests use the restrooms and drop litter. The guest panel shows their thoughts (the game's own lines, such as I can't wait to see some animals) and what they carry.

Guests now think with the game's own guest AI. They choose between watching animals, talking with each other, complaining when hungry and buying food: put a food stand near a path and hungry guests walk up to it, pay the stand price and carry their burger away. After watching an exhibit they react the way the original does, from cheering to covering their eyes, and when their departure points run out they walk back to the gate and leave.

Guests are here. While the zoo is open they come in through the front gate (by the original guest manager rules), pay admission from their own cash, walk the paths and stop at exhibits to watch the animals, then go home. Each one is one of the game's 15 everyday guest types with a random name and their own clothes, skin and hair. Click a guest for the original guest panel with their needs, cash and what they are doing. When a guest leaves, the zoo fame is worked out with the original formula, so the stars now move.
Zoo Status now has its graphs: monthly profit, donations, attendance and fame (in stars), as bars or a line, with the original axis labels. The zoo keeps a monthly record for them from now on.

The Zoopedia works: press the Zoopedia (book) button in any info or buy panel. All entries from the game and its expansions are in the contents tree on the left; pages show the original pictures, conservation status, biome and region maps, facts and links to other entries, with back, forward and home buttons. The zoo pauses while it is open.

Picking something to build now shows the original buy panel (picture, price, upkeep; for animals biome, home region and conservation status; rotate buttons for objects). Landscaping tools show the original brush size panel with - and + buttons. Animals have the family tree tab (mother, father, grandparents, siblings, mate, children; click one to select it). Build lists show two rows of small icons like the original.

The original in-game interface is now the default (no ?shell needed). New: the original Zoo Status window (zoo name, admission price, open or closed, money by category, balance sheet by month, fame bars), the Game Options menu (Save, Load, Return to Main Menu), each biome own water and ground brushes in Landscaping, cliff and ditch tools, and [ ] for the brush size. Build lists no longer offer the rubble of destroyed buildings. The old development menu is still there with ?classic.

Click an object in the original interface (?shell) to see its original info panel: animals show their picture, name (you can rename them), need icons coloured by state (green satisfied, yellow pressing, red critical), what they are doing, their biome, home region, conservation status and sex. A follow-camera button, release to the wild and put up for adoption work. Benches, food, plants and buildings get their own panels, and Sell asks with the original confirmation.

The main menu now opens when you start the game, over one of the 20 original backdrop pictures. In the local build a refresh brings you back to the zoo you were playing; New zoo starts a fresh zoo at once.

The original in-game interface is coming: open localhost:8080/?shell to try it. The bottom-left button panel, Construction, Animals and Landscaping panels with all their tabs and build lists, date bar with pause, fame stars and the cash bar all come from the game own files; picking an animal there and clicking the map adopts it.

Save and Load, with the original screens: save your zoo under a name (with a picture), load it later from the game or from the main menu Load/Save button, delete old saves. Saved games stay in this browser.

Main menu and map selection, in the original look: the game own layout files are now read and drawn (splash screen, main menu with the paw buttons, Freeform map selection with all maps, map picture, location, biome and size). Open localhost:8080 without ?map= to see it; the Menu button in the top bar brings it back.

Emoticons above animals, like the original (your request): the game own emoticon effects play when animals are happy, sick, hungry, mating, pregnant and more. Guests and staff will show theirs too when they arrive.
Debug buttons in the animal panel: Make unhappy / Make happy (local mode only), to try escapes and fights quickly.
Swimming: animals that swim in the original (polar bears, hippos...) go into deep water, swim and tread water with their head above the surface.
Sickness, as in the original: animals living in a dirty exhibit get sick, then very sick (and can pass it on), and die of illness if it goes on; good conditions heal them.
Food shows how full it is, like the original: meat dishes, hay and carcasses change from full to two thirds, one third and empty as animals eat.
Predators hunt: a lion sharing an exhibit with zebras stalks, chases and kills them; the zebra becomes a carcass the lions eat.

Escapes: unhappy animals now smash weak fences (buffalo through chain link), jump low fences (lions) or climb and dig under, with the original messages. A smashed fence shows its broken model and the animals walk out into the zoo.
Money: open the game once as localhost:8080/?money=9999999 to set your cash (as you asked).
The city and countryside around the zoo now sit at the same height as the zoo (your screenshot): they were placed 13 m too low, leaving a gap.
Female / Male choice when adopting an animal, with the original buttons (Female by default, like the original).

Breeding works with the original tasks and scripts: a female calls a male, they mate, she becomes pregnant and gives birth to 2-3 young; the young grow up into adults later. Parents no longer treat their own young as prey.
Animals now leave droppings (they were created but not shown, and stood on edge).
Fixed plants and trees drawn as solid green or dark cards (your screenshots): many materials take their see-through setting from the game effect files (effects/*.fx), which are now read.

Shelters were missing from the build menu: all 45 (caves, shade structures, stables, nests, burrows...) are back, plus 26 other objects whose models were not found before. Lions now rest and hide in a shade structure, play with toys and use a scratching post; happy animals unlock more activities, like in the original.

Exhibit suitability: each animal now feels its exhibit biome (terrain, plants and rocks, with the species own biome likes and dislikes) and whether there is enough space for the group. Animals and food levels are now kept when you reload.

Animals now think like the original: their needs (hunger, thirst, rest, social...) grow over time and they pick tasks from the game own AI files. Lions given a meat dish and a water dish walk over, eat with their real eating animations, drink, then pee and poop; zebras snort, groom, scratch and wander. Click an animal to see what it is doing and its top needs. Also: the sun now crosses the sky, and the camera uses the original field of view.

Lighting fix for all objects: glowing (emissive) material colour is now combined like the original Direct3D lighting, so colours are no longer washed out (the front gate elephant is grey, not pink). Scrolling textures (waving flags, flowing effects) now animate.

Phase 4 started: exhibits. Fenced areas are detected (straight and diagonal fences, the zoo wall), animals roam their whole exhibit and cannot walk through fences. Click an animal to see its exhibit size.

Zoo Status panel (click the stars next to the money): open or close the zoo and set the admission price. Found the original game logic scripts inside the game files and decoded the exact zoo fame formula (animals, species, happiness, education, entertainment, awards); it switches on with guests. Finance labels now match the original.

Finances: costs, refunds and monthly upkeep come from each object like the original (selling gives 80% back, not 50%). Click the money to see this and last month. Fixed 16 objects that showed the wrong model (gift shop, restaurant and small bathroom showed only a sign or effect). Objects with states (shop signs, bat cave bats) now show the right part.
Game clock with pause (P) and day and night: the original lights and sky dome change through the day, and the landscape around the map (hills, trees) is now shown.

New zoos now start like the original map: front gate, zoo wall, parking lot, entrance paths, trees and rocks. Fixed a model reader bug that dropped parts of 321 models (food stands, kiosks, the front gate and more). Models now load faster.
Paths now use the original edge masks (north_mask / west_mask), so path edges match the original texel pattern.
Undo / Redo (buttons and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) for placing, selling, fences, gates, paths and terrain edits.
Theme versions are now named apart, e.g. Cheesecake Cart (Classic / Jungle / Safari / Desert / Extinct / Endangered).
Expansion models now use their vertex colours and material colours (e.g. the cheesecake display was plain white).
Objects made of several parts: 164 objects (snack carts, photo booth, ...) now show their vendors (animated), signs, umbrellas and goods.
Placement rules from each object's ZTPlacementData: footprints, 45° rotation, grid snapping, no overlapping, water/land, ground levelling under buildings, green/red footprint preview.
Fix: see-through surfaces (fences, leaves, glass) turned whitish at a distance because the page showed through the canvas. Canvas is now opaque.
Original lighting from world/lights (per biome: ambient + sun, side and back lights). Textures now use the game files' own mipmaps.
Fences: 60 fence types in a Fences tab; drag from a tile corner to draw straight or diagonal fences; they follow hills; select a segment to sell it.
Build menu grew to 778 items (expansion objects in the .bfb format now load).
Water reworked to match the original: a brush that paints shallow or deep water onto the land (depths from each biome). Strength slider added for raise, lower, smooth and flatten.
Water tools added: Add water fills a hollow up to its rim, Remove water drains it; water type picked by biome. Phase 1 (terrain) complete.
Terrain tools added (Terrain tab): raise, lower, smooth, flatten, biome paint with ground cover. Edits saved per map; New zoo restores the original map.
Built an automated play-tester (tools/playtest.mjs) that clicks and drags in a real browser and takes screenshots.
Original maps load in the sandbox (map menu at the top). Ground painted with the game's own brush method on the graphics card; water regions shown.
All 138 terrain files parse (69 standard maps + scenarios): 0.75 m cells, 16 biomes.
Verified in the game data: escapes, attacks on guests, fleeing, rampages and recapture are all defined. Added to the feature list.
Wrote the full phase plan (15 phases, in the order a zoo is built).
All 107 animal species now load and animate, including Extinct Animals and Marine Mania (.bfb format decoded; 2,575 models, no errors).
Downloaded the OpenZT2 source (1,666 Rust files) as a read-only reference.
Fixed your OpenZT2 install: removed a mismatched 32-bit DLL, installed the official 64-bit MinGW runtime DLLs from MSYS2 (checksums verified, Defender clean).
Ghidra finished: zt.exe game code is encrypted by copy protection. Stopped that route; extracted 9,370 readable strings instead.
.bfb geometry verified on all 2,609 files.
You approved Ghidra; analysis of zt.exe started.
Ghidra Defender scan finished: no threats. Asked you for approval to run it.
Started decoding .bfb: 2,609 files, 19 vertex layouts, skeleton bone records identified.
74 of 107 species animate correctly in tests. The other 33 use the .bfb model format.
Animation playback added: skinning on the graphics card, walk/idle/extra actions, root motion removed so feet do not slide.
Verified the skinning formula against every animal model, and the animation units (millimetres, quaternions scaled by 10,000).
Created this progress page.
Checked the ZtModArchive repo: contains decompiled game Lua scripts, which are useful. Its .exe tools won't be run (unvetted).
Downloaded Ghidra 12.1.4 from the official GitHub; checksum verified; Defender scan started.
Animation format (.bf) decoded and verified against all animation files.
Sandbox mode built: map, camera, build menu, placing animals and objects.

rules: Each phase is finished and working before the next one starts.
Everything is checked against the original game, not just OpenZT2.
Smooth performance on PC and phones is part of every phase: fewer draw calls, level-of-detail models, culling of off-screen objects, loading in the background, lighter textures on phones.
Every model, animation and data file is tested automatically before you see it.
